contracts.representation: GET /v1/storefront/:handle?projection=render-v1 opts into one canonical effective raw template_config plus compact release metadata. Default response remains the existing shape. Unknown/duplicate projection and unrecognized compact query inputs refuse before cache/DB. Distinct fallback bundle aliases and all other manifest activation/metadata stay intact; remove only structurally equal earlier candidates.
contracts.selection: Match current mapper precedence: nonempty record(template_snapshot || release_config), else nonempty manifest.templateConfig, else site.template_config; no demo substitution introduced. Original fallback/localization/appearance/runtime validation remain app-owned.
contracts.release: Derive release ID/version from the published site record; query matching store and pinned release. A concurrent publication marks the old immutable row superseded (migration366), so a pinned row may be published or superseded but must have a publication timestamp, matching ID/store/version and no deletion. Missing/mismatched/unreadable mandatory release is sanitized unavailable, never mutable-theme fallback. Genuine verified no-release legacy state keeps its existing config fallback. Live store/status lookup must also distinguish a verified missing row from a transport/database failure; no false404 on unreadable dependency. Existing verified legacy/manifest-only configuration fallback precedence remains supported; an unreadable or missing pinned release never authorizes that fallback.
contracts.dataWork: One store/release/app-block population, fixed projections, no broad search or migration. Compact SQL selects one coalesced snapshot and required manifest/metadata rather than redundant artifact fields; REST selects snapshot and only fetches legacy release_config when needed. Record actual query fields/cardinality and response bytes; do not equate smaller response with eliminated DB IO. The live store record still includes its legacy config because legacy fallback semantics require it; do not claim all DB byte cost is removed. Internal projection cost and remaining store/config overhead must be recorded.
contracts.cache: Load the live published site before Cache API lookup and refuse explicit published=false. Include a digest of the complete site snapshot (including release pointer/version and appearance/config) in the existing bootstrap cache key, with projection query separating shapes. This prevents in-flight pre-publish producers filling the current key after purge. Legacy rows without a stable release pointer bypass Cache API. External response no-store preserves the live check; internal content-keyed public cache retains its normal bounded TTL. Existing legacy purge paths remain; no KV eventual-consistency dependency added. Prove native default/compact HIT separation, subsequent publication values and warmed unpublished refusal.
contracts.compatibility: Old SDK/mobile APIs and default payload continue; new SDK may receive old legacy payload from an old Gateway and app retains existing legacy mapping. Unsupported response projection fails closed. Private draft capability/resource endpoints remain full and independently verified.
contracts.verification: Tenant-core selection/deep JSON equality/key-order/distinct fallback/nonmutation; real Worker/owned PostgreSQL both SQL and REST paths for released/no-release/draft/missing/foreign/mismatched pointer and release outage/recovery; native normal merchant publication and all10presets/variant/image/COD/account lifecycle; previous9-sample profile as baseline, matched final9 samples with bytes/count/error conditions and timing caveats.
